vulnerabilities.description: Command injection risk: Uses execSync with string concatenation (newArgs.join(' ')) without proper shell escaping. Malicious input in argument values could break out and execute arbitrary commands.
Insecure data storage: JSON file stored without file permissions validation. Sensitive data written to disk in plaintext and readable by any user on the system (depending on umask).

Weak session identifier generation: Uses Date.now() for session IDs (sessionId format: 'session-{timestamp}'). Timestamps are predictable and can be enumerated by attackers to predict valid session IDs.

Insecure temporary file creation: Temporary files created with mode based on default umask without explicitly setting 0600 permissions. Other users may be able to read sensitive content (body text, GitHub tokens, etc.).
Insufficient input validation: No validation on 'key' parameter. Could allow path traversal attempts like '../../../etc/passwd' if this utility is exposed to untrusted input.
Unencrypted sensitive data: Session context object stores arbitrary data without encryption. If sessions contain authentication tokens or personal information, they are exposed in plaintext.
Inadequate error handling: Exceptions during writeFileSync or execSync may bypass the finally block cleanup, leaving temporary files with sensitive content on disk.
Directory creation without permission validation: mkdirSync called without mode parameter, uses default permissions. Should explicitly set restrictive permissions (0700).
Hardcoded sensitive agent list: Agent capabilities mapping is hardcoded. While not directly exploitable, exposing internal agent types could enable social engineering or reconnaissance.

recommendations: Replace execSync with proper shell escaping using the 'shell-escape' package or use spawn() with arguments array instead of string concatenation
Implement restrictive file permissions (0600) for all temporary files and persistent storage using fs.writeFileSync options: {mode: 0o600}
Replace plaintext storage with encrypted secrets using 'crypto' module; use authenticated encryption (AES-256-GCM)
Generate cryptographically secure session IDs using crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') instead of timestamps
Validate all key inputs against a whitelist pattern to prevent path traversal: /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/
Add proper exception handling to ensure cleanup happens in all error paths (use try-finally consistently)
Implement directory creation with restrictive mode: fs.mkdirSync(path, {recursive: true, mode: 0o700})
Add input sanitization layer for memory.js to prevent storing sensitive data in plaintext
Implement session expiration and automatic cleanup of old session files
Consider using a dedicated secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) instead of local file storage
